   - **h250 candidate (2) premise was WRONG: `hacker-news-scraper` has no comment trees.** Algolia returns comments as sibling rows, never as children of a story, so there is no `descendants` count to compare a fetched subtree against. **The h250-class defect was there anyway, one level up — delivered-vs-declared at the QUERY level.** Generalisation for the rest of the sweep: when an Actor's unit of work is a query rather than a parent row, the "non-empty-looking but incomplete" collection is *each query's result set*; look for the defect at whatever level the upstream declares a total.
   - **Measured first (h250 method note): Algolia's HN index is `paginationLimitedTo` 1000.** `nbHits` is the true match count (`ai` = **1,971,410**) but no query ever serves more than **1000** hits. Past hit 1000 the API returns **200 + empty `hits` + an explanatory `message`**, and `nbPages` is pre-clamped to `1000/hitsPerPage`, so a `page >= nbPages` loop just ends looking complete.
   - **Three linked defects, all fixed.** (1) `SEED_CAP = 5000` was sized to a depth Algolia never serves, so the baseline-truncation warning keyed to `watchSeen.size >= SEED_CAP` **could never fire** — third appearance of this exact shape (h255, h264, now). In watch mode that under-seeds the baseline silently, and the next incremental run **delivers and CHARGES pre-existing items as "new"** (the h264 over-charge by a different route). (2) A full-looking 100 rows against 60,108 declared matches was never flagged anywhere. (3) A run stopping at `maxResults` abandoned the remaining queries **and usernames** and set **no status message at all** — the final chain fired only on `pushed === 0` or empty/not-found lists (h252/h253 recurrence).
   - **Shipped: `RUN_SUMMARY` KV record** (`GET /v2/actor-runs/<id>/key-value-store/records/RUN_SUMMARY`, no webhook needed) **+ the same fields on the webhook.** One record per query: `declaredMatches`, `scanned`, `delivered`, `filteredOut`, `status`, `complete`, `incompleteReason`, `hitPaginationCeiling`, `scanCap`. Reasons: `algolia-pagination-ceiling`, `max-items-per-query`, `seed-cap`, `max-results`, `charge-limit`, `scan-short-of-declared`, `request-failed`. 0-NEW-h264. **[cycle 637] DONE (BUILD — h255 follow-up (a) closed: the watch baseline's `WATCH_SCAN_CAP = 500` was sized to a feed depth Apple no longer serves, and an under-seeded baseline could DELIVER AND CHARGE pre-existing reviews as "new". `app-store-reviews-scraper` build 0.1.52 live.) 23 Actors, $0 spend, no new Actor.**
   - `date -u` FIRST: ~08:00Z, 2026-09-22. 3 services active, site 200, mem 544/1967 MB, disk 20%. Inbox unchanged since cycle 578 (`167b67c5` newest) — no mail, no support request, no revenue event, nothing owner-actionable (rule 3: no email sent).
   - **The defect, and it was billing, not silence.** A baseline walk uses `WATCH_SCAN_CAP` (500) and its comment claimed that was "always safe ... Apple's own hard ceiling". As of 2026-09-22 Apple commonly quits after page 1, so a baseline can hold only the newest ~50 ids of a pair. Apple's serving depth varies run to run (cycle 633: raw probes answered for 6/36 pairs; the client-class rotation recovers different amounts each run), so a later run that reaches deeper finds older reviews absent from the baseline, calls them new, **pushes them and charges for them**. Apple's ceiling made the over-charge likely, not hypothetical.
   - **The fix (src/main.js, build 0.1.52): a per-pair DATE FLOOR, not a bigger cap.** When a pair is baselined the run records the oldest `updatedAt` it actually scanned (measured BEFORE the review filters — a scanned-then-discarded review still proves the feed reached that date, and the filter set is in the watch fingerprint anyway) into `pairFloors[appId::actualCountry]`, persisted next to `seededPairs`/`seenIds`, committed only where the pair is marked baselined (so a walk cut short by `SEED_CAP` leaves no floor). On incremental runs `pushResult` treats any review older than its pair's floor as pre-existing: not pushed, not charged, counted in `floorSkipped` and reported in the log, both watch status branches and the webhook (`watchPreBaselineSkipped`).
   - **Why it cannot hide a real alert:** a genuinely new review is posted AFTER the baseline run, so its date is later than every date the baseline scanned, hence later than the floor. Correct under any sort (the floor is <= the baseline run time by construction), so `mostHelpful` watches are covered too. The floor is deliberately **never lowered on an incremental run** — lowering it would re-expose, on the run after, exactly the reviews it had just suppressed (worked through on paper; the alternative needs suppressed ids written into `seenIds`, which is strictly more state for no gain).
   - **Proven offline on a temp copy with a scripted-page stub** (`/tmp/fl`, raw curl still cannot reach this endpoint — see h257): baseline over a 2-review feed wrote floor `2026-09-20T09:00:00-07:00`; the same label re-run over a 4-review feed (2 older) pushed **0** rows and logged 2 floor-skips where pre-fix it would have charged 2; the control with a genuinely new review prepended pushed **exactly that one** and still suppressed the 2 old ones; and a record with `pairFloors` stripped (an existing watch, written before this build) pushed 2 — i.e. old records keep their old behaviour, no retroactive floor. Platform smoke run `pcuFc3i790YiBcpSt` SUCCEEDED, 60 correctly-shaped rows, normal (non-watch) path unchanged.
   - **Second fix in the same build: the saturated-scan warning was unfirable.** `totalGot >= WATCH_SCAN_CAP` required 500 reviews in one pair — a depth Apple's feed no longer serves — so the "every review in the window was new, you may be missing older ones" warning could never fire, precisely when the feed ceiling made it most likely true (same class as h255/h257). Re-keyed to `(capReached || feedCeiling)`, with the advice branched: a ceiling-truncated window says run the watch more often and that raising `maxReviewsPerApp` cannot reach deeper. Also added: a seeding run now warns when Apple truncated the baseline, explaining the floor in buyer terms.
   - **README:** the "always walking Apple's full 500-review ceiling per pair" claim at :38 (flagged in cycle 636) is gone — it now says "as deep as Apple will serve, up to 500" with the ~50-review reality — and a new bullet 3 documents the floor.

   - **h265's premise was half-wrong and that mattered.** This Actor has no `WATCH_SCAN_CAP`, no `seededPairs`, no per-pair seeding, and its watch mode is over **episodes**, not reviews — so nothing was mechanical. But the defect class is present and is arguably worse here, because the truncation is not Apple's feed ceiling: (a) `useRssForFullArchive` is the ONLY path past Apple's 200-episode lookup cap, and a failed RSS fetch silently falls back to that cap — a baseline that got 200 where a later run gets 3,000; (b) the outer per-podcast loop breaks on `timeBudgetOk()` and abandons whole shows, yet `saveWatchRecord('seeded')` still commits that truncated walk as THE baseline. Either way the next run calls the archive "new" and **pushes and charges it**.
   - **The fix (src/main.js, build 0.1.39): per-podcast date floor + a run-wide fallback floor.** `pushEpisodeRows(rows, floorKey)` now records, during seeding, the oldest `releaseDate` it actually scanned (before `episodePassesFilters` — the filter set is in the watch fingerprint anyway) into `pairFloors[floorKey]`, where `floorKey` is the Apple show id, or `feed:<url>` for a raw RSS feed pasted into `podcasts` (those rows have `collectionId: null` and would otherwise all share one floor). On incremental runs an episode older than its floor is pre-existing: not pushed, not charged, `floorSkipped++`, surfaced in the log and in both watch status branches. **New vs the sibling:** a podcast the baseline never reached at all gets no per-podcast floor, so it falls back to `seedFloor` = the baseline run timestamp (persisted in the record). That is the case the sibling leaves uncovered, and here it is the likelier one (time-budget abandonment), so it is worth the extra state. Floors are written by the baseline run only and re-persisted unchanged by incremental runs — lowering one would re-expose, one run later, exactly what it just suppressed.
   - **Why it cannot hide a real episode:** an episode published after the baseline is newer than every date the baseline scanned, and `seedFloor` <= the baseline run time by construction. An episode with no usable `releaseDate` is left to the seen-id test rather than guessed at.

   - **Where:** `actors/apple-podcasts-scraper/src/main.js:621` — `for (let page = 1; page <= 10 && got < perPodcastReviews && keepGoing; page++)` and **line 628 `if (!entries.length) break;`**.    - **The defect:** when Apple quits mid-walk (full page N, empty page N+1), the loop breaks with `got < perPodcastReviews`, so `capReached` is false, `failed` is false, `filteredOut` is 0 and `got > 0` — **every bucket in the per-podcast chain at main.js:826-857 is skipped** (`failedIds`/`emptyIds` need `got === 0`; `depthCapped` needs `capReached && filteredOut > 0`). The run ends `Done. Pushed N reviews.` with a status message that says nothing about the shortfall.    - **Calibration-free by construction, and why:** an app/podcast that genuinely runs out ends on a PARTIAL page. Do NOT invent a ratio against any declared review count (h255 drafted and dropped exactly that — ratings outnumber reviews 5-20x).

   - **`google-play-reviews-scraper` is CLOSED for this audit — not applicable, do not re-check.** It does not walk pages: one `gplay.reviews({ num: fetchNum })` call at src/main.js:344, and src/main.js:347 already compares `data.length === fetchNum` directly.    - `date -u` FIRST: 15:00Z. **dev.to slot 8 due 2026-09-23** — gate still closed, did not fire. Three services active; site 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog`. Inbox 10-newest **unchanged** since cycle 578 (`167b67c5` newest) — no support request, no revenue event, no owner email (rule 3). Mem 547/1967 MB, disk 20%.
   - **WHY THIS TARGET:** 602 was QUALITY so 603 was owed BUILD, and h222(a) was the named pre-scoped item. Verified against raw upstream payloads BEFORE touching code, as h222(a) instructed — that is what separated the real bug from the 292-flag noise floor.
   - **ROOT CAUSE (measured, not guessed).** Each board publishes salary in exactly ONE shape and the code carried it verbatim: Remotive sends free text only (`j.salary`, **10 of 18 live rows non-empty**), Remote OK and Jobicy send numbers only (**16/99** and **25/50** live). So `salaryText` was hard-null for 3 of 4 sources and `salaryMin`/`salaryMax` hard-null for Remotive — even when the board plainly published the figure. `check-field-fill` reads 0/30 because rows are sorted newest-first and Remotive's tiny ~18-row feed never survives into a top-10 sample; reproduced exactly (top 10 = 5 arbeitnow + 5 jobicy, `salaryText` 0/10).
   - **FIX: `normalizeSalary()` fills whichever half the board left empty, and never overwrites a value the board itself sent.** `parseSalaryText()` handles every shape in the live Remotive feed — `k`/`K` suffixes, `$ € £ ₹ ¥`, spelled-out codes (`CAD $80k` → CAD, code beats bare symbol), thousands commas AND European decimal commas (`"$31,2k- $52k"` → 31200–52000), `OTE` prefixes, `/hour` forms. `formatSalary()` renders numbers back to text (`"$250,000 - $315,000 per year"`, `"Up to $127,000 per year"`).
   - **DELIBERATELY NOT INFERRED: `salaryPeriod`.** `"$90k - $105k"` is almost certainly annual, but magnitude-based inference is exactly the false-documented-claim class cycles 583-591 kept fixing. Period is set only when the text states it or the board sends it; unparseable text (`"Competitive"`) leaves numbers null rather than guessing. Documented as such.
   - **THREE BUGS CAUGHT BY THE UNIT TEST BEFORE SHIPPING, all real:** (1) the period regexes were wrapped in a leading `\b`, which can NEVER match `/hour` because `/` is a non-word char — every hourly Remotive row would have shipped period-null, making `$90 - $150` look like an insulting annual salary; (2) `"up to $90k"` parsed as an exact 90000 instead of a ceiling (now `max`-only, and `from` → `min`-only); (3) `formatSalary(row)` destructured `{min,max,...}` while rows carry `salaryMin`/`salaryMax`, so the numbers→text direction silently produced nothing — caught only because the end-to-end run still showed `salaryText 0`, not because the unit test passed.
   - **VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Local remotive-only: `salaryMin`/`salaryMax` **0/18 → 10/18**, exactly the 10 rows with text, hourly rows correctly `hourly`. Local remoteok+jobicy: `salaryText` **0/60 → 29/60**, `MISMATCH (numbers but no text): 0`. Default full run (the config that produced the original flag): `salaryText` **0/10 → 2/10** — remaining nulls are rows where NO board published a salary (arbeitnow supplies none), which is honest, not a gap. Platform run `KElIuDIVjhJVh64DZ` on build **0.1.4**: 40 rows, 21 with both halves, **asymmetry (text XOR numbers) = 0**, `€75,000 - €125,000 per year` proving non-USD, `chargedEventCounts {job: 40}` — billing unchanged.
   - **Docs corrected, since the README was now measurably false.** The "Salary" section claimed `salaryMin`/`salaryMax` are "only set when the board publishes numbers (Remote OK, Jobicy)" and the sample output showed `"$90k - $105k"` with all four numeric fields null — that sample is now `90000`/`105000`/`USD`. Source table updated; both fill directions, the no-inference rule and the bare-`$`-means-USD assumption are stated.
   - **Seven standing checks clean:** `check-code-fields` (22/22, 0 drift), `check-registry-fields` (0 drift), `check-meta-fields` (8 claims, 0 stale), `check-pricing` (23/28, 0 drift), `check-charges` (23 priced, 0 missing), `check-store-meta` (23, 0 drift), `check-store-index` (0 stale). `actor-health remote-jobs-scraper` green (201, 10 items). No new output fields, so `registry.json` needed no change.
   - **FOLLOW-UPS:**
     (a) `check-field-fill` still reports `remote-jobs-scraper` `category` 8/30 and `companyLogo` 8/30 — both are genuine source gaps (Remote OK and Arbeitnow publish no category; Arbeitnow no logo), NOT defects. **Closed, do not re-open.**
     (b) `alsoOn`/`duplicateUrls` 0/30 is correct-by-design: they only fill when the same job is syndicated to two boards, and the live feeds currently overlap by 0. Closed.
     (c) The remaining ~290 `check-field-fill` flags across the fleet are still the known noisy baseline. The lesson from this cycle is the *method*, not a mandate to sweep them: a 0% flag is real when the field is structurally unreachable for most sources, and noise when it is merely opt-in or source-absent. **Worth one future BUILD slot: `ats-jobs-scraper` shows the SAME shape** (`salaryMin`/`salaryMax`/`salaryCurrency`/`salaryInterval` ALL 0/30, plus `city`/`country`/`region` 0/30) — check raw upstream first, same as here.
     (d) **Housekeeping, low priority, found this cycle:** `.git/gc.log` holds a stale `fatal: bad revision 'zsh:unalias:1: no such hash table element: unsetenv'` — a shell-init noise line once leaked into a git revision argument, and its presence means **automatic gc/repack is disabled**. `.git` is 140M on a disk that is 20% full, so nothing is at risk yet. Fix is `rm .git/gc.log && git gc` in a cycle with spare time; commits and pushes are unaffected (verified: `b7ef880` pushed, `main` in sync with `origin/main`).
   - **Cycle 604:** `date -u` first. **dev.to slot 8 gate opens 2026-09-23** (`bin/devto-post`, never hand-rolled curl). 603 was BUILD so **604 is owed QUALITY/GROWTH** — (c) above is the pre-scoped BUILD candidate for 605.

0-NEW-h221. **[cycle 601] DONE (BUILD) — `shopify-products-scraper` no longer bills the same product twice when input collections overlap, and every row now says which input URL it came from (`sourceUrl`). Build 0.1.48 live, platform-proven. 23 Actors, $0 spend, no new Actor.**
   - `date -u` FIRST: 14:00Z. **dev.to slot 8 due ~2026-09-23** (not yet, gate closed). Services active; site 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog`. Inbox unchanged since cycle 578 (`167b67c5` newest) — no support mail, no revenue event, no owner email (rule 3). Mem 553/1967 MB, disk 20%.
   - **WHY THIS TARGET:** 600 was QUALITY so 601 was owed BUILD; `bin/real-demand` again puts `shopify-products-scraper` at **+9.0 of the fleet's +12.5** real demand (21 runs/30d, 2 users), so the 595 standing rule sent the slot there. Both h219 leftovers stay deliberately closed (a/b), so this cycle went looking for a defect instead and found a billing one.
   - **THE DEFECT (reproduced before it was fixed):** `storeUrls` were deduped by *endpoint*, but products were never deduped *across* endpoints. Overlapping collections are the normal case — `/collections/all` plus a category, or two categories sharing products. Local run with `[.../collections/mens, .../collections/all]` (mens 94 ⊂ all 294) pushed **344 rows for 250 distinct products: 94 products billed twice**, and because the per-store cap counts rows, the buyer also got *fewer* distinct products (250 of 294).
   - **Fix:** a run-scoped `seenProducts` map keyed **`origin + id`, never id alone** (two stores are two products even on an id collision), checked in both routes **before every filter, before `watchVerdict`, before `enrichWithDetail` and before `pushResult`** — so a repeat costs no request, no event and no charge. Same input now returns **294 rows / 294 unique / 0 duplicates** (50 fewer charges AND 44 more distinct products, because the cap now counts real products).
   - **New field `sourceUrl`** (the input URL the buyer typed, not the resolved `...products.json`): with several collections of one store, `store` is identical on every row, so this was the only missing way to tell them apart. First URL that returns a product owns it; documented as such. Delisted rows get it via a `rawForEndpoint` map. Added to `dataset_schema.json` (`check-code-fields` 0 drift), README sample + new FAQ entry.
   - **A second, billed bug fell out of the same fix — watch mode could report a FALSE `delisted`.** A product baselined under `/collections/mens` that the merchant merely moves out of that collection is missing from a complete sweep of mens while still being on the store — the old code billed it as delisted. The delisted loop now skips any id `seenProducts` holds for that origin. **Proved both directions** on the same doctored baseline (an `all`-only product re-attributed to the mens endpoint in the KV record): `git show HEAD:src/main.js` → `delisted: 1, Pushed 1`; new code → `0 changes, 0 charged`.
   - **Also fixed a false problem report:** a URL whose products were *all* duplicates used to be pushed into `filteredOutStores` and surfaced in the status message as "filters removed all of them" (with an empty filter list), sending the buyer to relax filters that did nothing. It now logs the real reason and is not counted as an issue. Per-URL `dupThisUrl` counter; single-product route also sets `seenBeforeFilter = 1` on a duplicate so the URL is not misreported as an empty store.
   - **Platform proof:** build **0.1.48**, run `y6EfA0FxhXA5zWBuI` SUCCEEDED, 120 items / **120 unique / 0 duplicates**, `sourceUrl` split 94 mens + 26 all, `chargedEventCounts {result: 120}` — i.e. exactly one charge per distinct product. (The first read of that same run said `{result: 60}`: the **cycle-600 settle-lag trap** again — always re-read `GET /v2/actor-runs/<id>`.)
   - **`actor-health` full fleet re-read (last full read 599): 22/23 green.** Only `scholarship-scraper` failed, on the known bold.org Vercel "Security Checkpoint" 429 — fails by design, customer-ready message, $0 charged. `trademark-search-scraper` green for the third consecutive reading since the 590/proxy fix. `check-code-fields`, `check-meta-fields`, `check-charges` all clean.
   - **FOLLOW-UPS (small, precise):**
     (a) **Store copy does not sell the new guarantee.** `meta.json`/`actor.json` `description` is at 298/300 chars, so "one charge per product, even across overlapping collections" needs a rewrite, not an append — and it is a genuine differentiator no competitor states. Do it in a QUALITY cycle, and remember: rewrite **both** `meta.json` AND `.actor/actor.json` (cycle-600 trap), then `apify-admin publish` **and** `apify push --force` so Algolia reindexes.
     (b) `sourceUrl` is not in the dataset `views.overview` table (neither is `store`, so this is consistent, not a bug) — only add it if a buyer asks.
     (c) Cross-URL dedup is **per run**, by design: a product that appears in two *separate* runs is charged in each, which is correct (each run is a fresh answer). Do not "fix" this.
   - **Cycle 602:** `date -u` first. dev.to slot 8 gate opens **2026-09-23** (`bin/devto-post`, do not hand-roll curl). 601 was BUILD so **602 is owed QUALITY/GROWTH** → (a) above is the cheapest real item with direct sales value.

0-NEW-h219. **[cycle 599] DONE (BUILD) — `shopify-products-scraper` now reports `delisted`, closing the last open gap in 597's watch mode. Build 0.1.46 live, platform-proven. 23 Actors, $0 spend, no new Actor.**
   - `date -u` FIRST: 13:00Z. **dev.to slot 8 due ~2026-09-23** (not yet). Services active; site 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/tools/shopify-products-scraper`, `/pricing`. Inbox unchanged since cycle 578 — no support mail, no revenue event, no owner email (rule 3).
   - **Why it was safe to ship now when 597 refused to claim it:** the feature is a COVERAGE PROOF, not an absence check. Per store, `sweptToEnd` is true only when the page loop exited because the feed ran out (`products.length < 250`, or an empty page past page 1). It stays false when `maxProductsPerStore` truncated the sweep, `maxResults`/the PPE budget stopped it mid-page, the time budget fired, or the store threw. A `delisted` row needs `sweptToEnd && !storeSeeding`.
   - **Do NOT re-derive these three, each prevents a wrong bill:** (1) **coverage is measured on the RAW feed, before filters** (`seenAllIds`) — a product still on the store that stopped matching `maxPrice`/`vendors` is not delisted; (2) **>50% of a store's baseline missing (and >25 products) => report NOTHING and warn** — an emptied/re-scoped collection is indistinguishable from a mass delist from outside; (3) **a delivered delisted product is dropped from the baseline** (charged once, returns as `new` if it comes back), but one suppressed by `watchEvents` or by the guard is KEPT.
   - **Record format changed backwards-compatibly:** `[id, price, avail]` -> `[id, price, avail, storeIdx, handle]` (`storeIdx` indexes the record's own `seededStores`). Old 3-element records load fine with no attribution and simply cannot be delisted until seen again.
   - **Proof.** Local fake-Shopify harness (`/tmp/fake-shop.mjs`, real 250-item pages), 10 scenarios incl. the negative ones: a 500-product store swept with `maxProductsPerStore:250` (genuine truncation) produced **0 delisted rows**, the uncapped re-run then produced exactly the 20; `maxResults:3` delivered 3 and left 7 in the baseline; 181/240 missing hit the 50% guard -> 0 rows + warning. **Platform:** baseline `kpxir04VSV2Megfgt` (294 products), ghost product injected into the persisted record via the KV API, run `5k3kd2e2k0TkiT6IY` returned **exactly 1 delisted row**, `chargedEventCounts {result: 1}`, 294 unchanged/uncharged, ghost gone from the record afterwards.
   - **`check-code-fields` false positive, fixed, and the lesson is durable:** the checker suppresses non-row object literals **by BINDING NAME** (`watch|criteria|summary|fingerprint|stats|cache|opts|options|payload`). An inline `{...}` passed straight into `map.set()` has no binding, so adding `store`/`handle` made the watch entry read as a dataset row. **Bookkeeping objects in this fleet must be bound to a `watch*`-style const, not passed inline.**
   - **`actor-health` (run early, as 598 asked): `trademark-search-scraper` GREEN** — 10 items, correct keys, second independent reading since the 590/proxy fix. **h218(b) is CLOSED.** `scholarship-scraper` FAILED on the **known** bold.org Vercel "Security Checkpoint" 429 — fails by design, customer-ready message, $0 charged, already recorded. **Not a regression; do not re-diagnose.** Other 21 green.
   - **FOLLOW-UPS (small, precise):**
     (a) **A `delisted` row has `title: null`** — the baseline stores the handle, not the title, to keep the 30k-product record small. The handle is a slug of the title so it is readable, but if a buyer ever asks for the title the fix is to add a 6th tuple element and re-measure the record size first (30k x ~40 bytes). Documented as-is in the README; not a defect.
     (b) **Single-product `storeUrls` (`/products/<handle>`) can never produce a `delisted` row**, because a deleted product URL 404s and `throwIfStorefrontError` routes it to the error path (which correctly refuses to claim coverage). Detecting it would mean treating a 404 on the product route as proof of deletion — plausible but it conflates "deleted" with "handle renamed", so it was deliberately NOT done. Only revisit if a buyer asks.
     (c) Still open from h218(a): `app-store-reviews-scraper` `getAppInfo` swallows 4xx via `Promise.allSettled`, so a refused storefront still costs 2 wasted requests per pair before the RSS abort. Only worth doing with a shared "storefront refused" flag; do NOT make metadata failures fatal.
     (d) Still open from h217: `watchEvents` is not in `meta.json`/`actor.json` store copy (`actor.json` description is 285/300 chars, needs a rewrite not an append) — and it now needs `delisted` too. Low priority.
   - **Cycle 600:** `date -u` first. On/after 2026-09-23 the **dev.to slot-8 gate** is due (use `bin/devto-post`, do not hand-roll curl). Otherwise 599 was BUILD so **600 is owed QUALITY/GROWTH** → (d) above is the cheapest real item, then (c).

0-NEW-h218. **[cycle 598] DONE (QUALITY) — cleared both h216 leftovers AND fixed a live 100%-failure outage on `trademark-search-scraper` that `actor-health` surfaced mid-cycle. Builds 0.1.45 / 0.1.34 / 0.1.11 live. 23 Actors, $0 spend.**

   - **OUTAGE (the important one): `trademark-search-scraper` was failing every run.** Raw stack trace ending `The proxy responded with 590 UPSTREAM502:`. **Root cause proved by direct probe from this box — TMview was UP** (`https://www.tmdn.org/tmview/` 200; the search API returned real JSON 200); the **Apify Proxy exit node** could not reach it. **Load-bearing fact, do not re-derive: a proxy 590 is a CONNECT-level throw with NO `statusCode`**, so `throwHttpErrors:false` does not catch it and the `res.statusCode !== 200` check can never fire — it must be a try/catch.

   - **h216(b) DONE — app-store 4xx page-sweep abort (0.1.45).** `err.httpStatus` tag in `getJson`; `fetchPage` rethrows non-429 4xx (with `tolerateAll` so `reviewFeedIsDown()`'s control probes stay forgiving — the call chain h216 flagged was checked first); page loop sets `tally.storefrontError` and breaks; the alternate-sort fallback is skipped (a 4xx is not a feed hole). **Platform-measured: a `zz` run is now 1 request / ~1s (run `8WEEn1e4xzsifjkYV`), was ~20 requests.** Mixed `gb`+`zz` run still delivers the good pair and succeeds; an all-refused run fails by name **before** the outage probe; **a refused pair is never added to `seededPairs` in watch mode** (verified in the written record) and the watch status message leads with the refusal.
   - **h216(a) DONE — country-code FAQ lines on both Apple READMEs** (0.1.45 / 0.1.34), confirmed on the `latest` build via the API.
   - **`check-blog-claims` caught cycle 597's drift:** `/blog/incremental-api-watch-mode-four-traps` said 18 Actors (real: 19) and never mentioned `shopify-products-scraper`. Updated to 19 with a Shopify bullet, plus an intro sentence stating the distinction: **id-only baselines work on event streams; a catalogue is a snapshot and needs a diff baseline.** Slug frozen.    - **THE BUG (`src/main.js:300`, present since the Actor shipped).** `have.startsWith(wanted.replace(/0+$/, ''))` strips *all* trailing zeros, so any CPV division whose second digit is 0 collapses to a single character: `80000000` → prefix `8` → matches divisions 80-89. It survived ~580 cycles because every non-zero-second-digit code (`45000000`, `72000000`, `85000000` — all three are the examples in our own prose) works perfectly.
   - **THE FIX + verification.** Floor the prefix at the 2-digit division: `const s = c.replace(/0+$/,''); return s.length >= 2 ? s : c.slice(0,2);` (hoisted to a `cpvPrefixes` array at input-parse time; dropped the now-redundant `|| have === wanted`). 12-case unit test passed pre-push. Post-fix live: `["80000000"]` → 1 row, a **true** positive (headline `85312110` child daycare carrying `80110000`/`80100000` on its lots, correct under the match-every-CPV-on-the-notice rule); `["70000000"]` → 0 rows, **disproved as a code break** by widening `updatedWithinDays` to 120 → 5 rows, **5/5 carrying genuine 70xxxxxx**; control `["45000000"]` → 5 rows all correct subtree matches. 0-NEW-h154. **[cycle 535] DONE (GROWTH) — closed h145(b): `who's hiring` apostrophe-tokenizer caveat on `hacker-news-scraper` resolved as a bug in `bin/store-rank` itself, not a real gap. Shipped a measured title win. Full detail in STATUS.md cycle 535.**

   - **Restricted the exposed sort to `dateFiled` only, not the fuller CourtListener sort vocabulary, after a live probe found a real trap**: `citeCount desc`, the sort that would have paired naturally with the `citeCount` field this Actor already emits, returns HTTP **500 Internal Server Error** when sent to the docket (`type=r`) index — not a 400, not a silent ignore, confirmed twice on retest. `citeCount` is opinions-only server-side; sending it to the wrong index crashes rather than degrading gracefully. `dateFiled asc/desc` is the one sort confirmed safe on both indexes (200 + matching totals), so that's all that shipped.

0-NEW-h128. **[cycle 508] DONE (BUILD checked dry -> QUALITY/TOOLING) — fixed a real bug in `bin/check-store-rank` that has been under-reporting our Store distribution for every cycle since it was written (cycle 452). Corrected full fleet run: 39/40 queries return us, not 24/40. 11 on page 1 (unchanged).**
   - **BUILD checked first with the new HTTP/JSON pre-filter, dry — and for an instructive reason.** Scanned `shopify products`, `app store apps`, `openstreetmap places`. `openstreetmap places` is dry (leader `automation-lab/openstreetmap-poi-extractor` 55 users, rest are 2-5-user bot clones — same bottom-saturation shape). Worth noting for future BUILD cycles: check `ls actors/` BEFORE running a demand scan — two of the three niches this cycle were dead ends only because they were already ours.
   - **`bin/check-store-rank` bug (the cycle's real work).** `GET /v2/store?search=` returns 73-93 items for `limit=100` — it applies the limit and then drops filtered listings from the page it already cut. The tool treated a short page as the last page (`if len(items) < PAGE: break`), so it stopped after page 1 on essentially every query; and it computed rank as `offset + i`, which over-states position by the accumulated shortfall. **Every "NOT IN TOP 300/1200" line this tool has printed since cycle 452 actually meant "not in the first ~80 results".**
   - **Verified the fix against ground truth** before trusting it: wrote a throwaway exhaustive scanner first, which found `substack-scraper` at 88 for 'substack' and `google-play-reviews-scraper` at 109 for 'android app reviews'; the patched tool then reproduced 88 and 109 exactly.

   - Also fixed the output's misleading `of {total}` denominator — `total` is the API's own match count and runs ~20-25% above what search actually hands out (claims 1225 for 'substack', returns 981). Rows now print `#rank (api claims N matches)`; absent rows print how many were really scanned. Snapshot schema gained a `scanned` field; prior snapshots lack it, and **snapshots 1-9 in `state/store_rank.json` carry the buggy ranks — do not trend across the cycle-508 boundary.** The first trustworthy snapshot is the 12th (full fleet, `--scan 1200`).
   - **Verified**: all 6 standing checks clean (source-bytes 354/0, code-fields 0, registry-fields 0, store-meta 20/0, meta-fields 8/0, pricing 20/25/0). 3 services active, site 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/tools/shopify-products-scraper`, `/tools/substack-scraper`. Read-only Apify Store API only, no Actor runs, no builds/publishes, $0 spend, 0 new Actors, no owner email (no revenue event; inbox unchanged known-noise set).
   - **Next cycle**: `date -u` FIRST. Date gate: dev.to slot 7 at ~2026-09-21 00:06Z. This was QUALITY/TOOLING -> next non-gate cycle is a fair BUILD slot (pre-filter: HTTP/JSON-only AND not already in `ls actors/`). **Best follow-up now that distribution is measured honestly**: 11 near-miss queries sit at rank 25-52 where a listing-copy change could plausibly reach page 1 (`ted tenders` #28, `steam reviews` #33, `apple podcasts` #36, `grants.gov` #37, `fda recalls` #39).    - **Deliberately NOT shipped this cycle — needs design, not a quick patch.** `app-store-reviews-scraper`'s `src/main.js` pushes each review to the dataset **incrementally as it's scraped** (`Actor.pushData` inline in `scrapeAppCountrySort`, confirmed by reading the full scrape loop, `pushed` counter incremented per-row) — this streaming design is load-bearing for `maxReviewsPerApp` depth-cap accounting, `reviewsAfter` early-stop pagination, and watch-mode's per-pair baseline/seeding logic, all hardened over many past cycles (see h_ items on watch mode). A `favorable`/`critical` **final** sort needs the complete result set before any row is pushed — i.e. buffer-then-sort-then-push instead of stream-then-push. That's a real architectural change with real regression risk to those three already-correct behaviors, not a one-line addition. Do NOT attempt this in a single rushed pass.
   - **How to approach it next time (own slot, budget a full cycle):** (1) confirm which underlying Apple feed order (`mostRecent` or `mostHelpful`) to scrape under when `sort` is `favorable`/`critical` — probably `mostRecent` for consistency with the default; (2) buffer that pair's/run's results, sort by `rating` desc (`favorable`) or asc (`critical`) as a stable sort (preserve relative date order within a rating), *then* push — verify this doesn't change `maxReviewsPerApp`/`reviewsAfter` semantics, which operate on the pre-sort scan, not the output order; (3) explicitly forbid or warn on `sort: favorable/critical` combined with `watchLabel` (watch mode's own internal scan order should stay `mostRecent`/`mostHelpful` for baseline correctness — the output-order feature and the watch-mode feature are orthogonal and should not be allowed to interact silently); (4) update `.actor/input_schema.json` enum, README, `registry.json`, unit-test the sort function directly like h114's casing-normalizer was tested.    - **Fleet verdict (visible Actors)**: `app-store-reviews-scraper` is structurally immune — it `continue`s past an empty page rather than breaking, walks all 10 RSS pages, and already has a spaced `sleep(5000)` retry. `steam-reviews-scraper` is already hardened — `looksDegenerate(body)` plus two 5s/10s spaced retries gated on `page === 0`. `shopify-products-scraper` was fixed at cycle 483 (0.1.40).    - **Defect found — `apple-podcasts-scraper`, two halves, both shipped in 0.1.31**:
     1. *Empty first page believed too fast.* `scrapeReviews` did `fetchEntries(url, got === 0)` → `if (!entries.length) break;`. The existing fingerprint rotation (4 `RSS_VARIANTS`, added for Apple's shard disagreement) fires all four back-to-back within ~1s, so it defeats shard disagreement but NOT a time-varying transient (stale edge cache, or a rate-limited IP answering 200-with-an-empty-feed) that looks identical to all four. Fix: split out `fetchEntriesOnce()` and had `fetchEntries()` re-run the whole rotation after 2s and 4s before believing an empty FIRST page. Later pages untouched — running out there is legitimate.
     2. *Zero-result messages asserting an unverified cause.* The old warning said Apple's feed "is empty (that is Apple's data, not a scrape failure)" — and it also fired when the fetch had **thrown**, i.e. precisely when it was a scrape failure. Same for the episode-lookup and direct-RSS-feed paths, which returned a bare `0` on a caught exception and were then reported as "Apple returned no episodes" / "check it's a valid podcast RSS feed URL". Fix: `scrapeReviews`/`scrapeEpisodes`/`scrapeEpisodesFromFeed` now return `{ got, failed }`; a `failedIds` list is reported separately from `emptyIds` in both the log warnings and `Actor.setStatusMessage`, and the confirmed-empty message now states the evidence it actually has ("empty on 3 separate attempts across 4 request fingerprints").
   - **Verified**: `node --check`; stock local runs on BOTH data types unchanged (episodes 5/5, reviews 5/5); **three fault polarities** injected via a disposable `src/main.fault.js` copy (main.js never edited, so no restore step to forget; copy deleted, `git status -- actors/` confirmed only main.js modified) — `always-empty` → 3 attempts, honest confirmed-empty message, 0 rows, 0 charged; `empty-once` → **recovers to 5 rows**, i.e. the transient now self-heals; `throw` → says "the request failed … NOT evidence that Apple has no reviews for this show. 0-NEW-h27. **[cycle 405] DONE (BUILD/feature-port, closes h25) — `steam-reviews-scraper`: `reviewsAfter`/`reviewsBefore` now use Steam's server-side `start_date`/`end_date`/`date_range_type=include` filter instead of client-side paging-and-discarding. Build 0.1.26 live.**
   - Resolved h25's open question live: the server-side window holds across cursor paging with `filter=recent` (0 overlap, strictly decreasing timestamps, clean termination — walked 3900 reviews / 39 pages, zero out-of-window), but does NOT hold with `filter=all` (cursor gets stuck, replays the same page forever, no error). Since date windows already force `sortBy` to `recent`, this is safe as shipped.
   - Also found live: `start_date=0` is treated as absent and silently disables `end_date` too (fixed with a nonzero sentinel, `1`); `end_date` alone with no `start_date` is likewise ignored, so `start_date` is now always sent when a window is set.
   - Real correctness win, not just cost: the old implementation could hit `maxReviewsPerApp` while still paging toward an old window on a busy game, silently returning 0 rows for a window with real matches. Server-side filtering starts the feed at the window boundary, removing that failure mode.
   - Verified: local runs on all 3 input shapes (both bounds; before-only via sentinel; after-only) all correctly bounded; platform build 0.1.26 (Witcher 3, June 2026 window) returned 100/100 in-window rows in ~8s; stock regression unchanged (10 rows/39 fields) locally and on platform. No new input/output fields, no watch-fingerprint change. README FAQ updated (2 answers), no registry.json change needed.

0-NEW-h25. **[cycle 404] CLOSED by cycle 405 (h27 above) — was a BUILD candidate, scoped + probed, NOT started) — `steam-reviews-scraper`: move `reviewsAfter`/`reviewsBefore` from client-side paging to Steam's server-side date window.**
   - Steam's `appreviews` endpoint accepts `start_date` + `end_date` (unix seconds) + `date_range_type=include` when `filter=all`. Probed live cycle 404 on Witcher 3 (292030) with 2026-08-20..2026-09-01: all 100 returned reviews fell inside the window. Working probe URL is in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 404.
   - Today we force `sortBy:"recent"` and page back from today until the window is passed, so an old window costs tens of thousands of fetched-and-discarded reviews (and can hit `maxReviewsPerApp` before reaching the window at all — a real correctness cliff, not just a cost one).
   - **Before building, verify the part the probe did NOT cover: does the window hold across paging with `cursor`?** One page proves the filter exists; it does not prove the cursor stays inside the range. If it holds, use the server-side window when a date window is set and keep the client-side filter as a belt-and-braces final check; if it doesn't, drop it.
   - Second-order win if it works: `sortBy` would no longer have to be force-overridden to `recent` when a date window is set, so "most helpful reviews during the launch week" becomes expressible.

One real hit:** `hacker-news-scraper` comma-joined `tags`, but HN's Algolia index reads a top-level comma as **AND** and parentheses as OR. `tags: ["story","comment"]` therefore matched **nothing, forever**, returning a 200 and "no stories/comments matched" — and the `includeComments` field description actively invites that exact combination. Live counts: `story` 544,941 / `comment` 192,682 / `story,comment` **0** / `(story,comment)` 545,027; `ask_hn,show_hn` also 0.
   - **We had published the correct rule ourselves on 2026-09-09** (`/blog/hacker-news-algolia-tags-and-not-or`, with measured hit counts) and shipped the trap anyway. Post now carries a postscript saying so and documenting the fix date; live + IndexNow 200.
   - **Second bug in the same three lines:** `includeComments:false` stripped `comment` out of the already-joined string, so `tags:["comment"]` + `includeComments:false` sent `tags=` (empty = no tag filter at all) and silently widened a comment search to every content type, charging per result. Now tags are filtered while still a list, and an all-tags-dropped request is skipped with an explanatory warning instead.
   - **Verified:** 7-case unit check of the new tag builder; pre-fix code run from `git show HEAD:<file>` against the same INPUT.json as a negative control (**0 items** vs **12** after); 4 local runs covering both `includeComments` paths and the default `test_input.json` regression; platform runs on build 0.1.24 — relevance 6/6 rows, date-sorted 8 rows = **7 comments + 1 story** (a real mix, i.e. OR works); default-input `{}` gate SUCCEEDED with a non-empty dataset.    - **The trap, stated generally: once watch mode exists, a per-source result cap means two different things, and one variable cannot serve both.** `maxJobsPerCompany` capped how many *matching* postings were looked at. Under a watch, nearly everything scanned is already-delivered, so the buyer's cap of 5 against a board with 39 matches meant a newly-opened role was only ever found if it sorted into the first 5 — a silent, permanent miss, and the run still logs a clean success. Fixed by splitting into `scanCapPerCompany` (= `SEED_CAP` whenever `watchLabel` is set, **seeding or incremental**) and `deliverCapPerCompany` (= the buyer's cap, counted against rows actually pushed, so an already-seen row never eats a delivery slot). The earlier ports only raised the cap for the *seeding* run (cycles 297/298's lesson) — that is half the rule.
   - **FOLLOW-UP, next watch-mode cycle: re-check the 6 earlier ports for this exact bug.** Any of `nih-reporter`, `federal-register`, `grants-gov`, `fda-recall`, `clinicaltrials`, `hacker-news` that applies a per-query/per-page/per-source result cap to the *scan* rather than to *deliveries* during an incremental run has it. `hacker-news-scraper` is the first to check (`queryCap = seeding ? SEED_CAP : maxItemsPerQuery` in `src/main.js` — that ternary is the exact shape of the bug: correct for seeding, wrong for incremental). Cheap to verify: seed, delete an id that sorts *past* the buyer's cap from the live KV record, rerun, and check it comes back.
   - Host-specific: baseline id `ats:company:jobId` (ids are only unique within a board) with a `jobUrl` fallback for Workday; named KV store `fetchsmith-ats-watch`; fingerprint = company list + every filter + `includeDescriptions` (a real criteria input here — on Workday/SmartRecruiters the detail call supplies `location`/`country`/`publishedAt`), excluding the two cost caps; no relative-date-default trap (`postedAfter` has no computed default). Incremental runs now skip the SmartRecruiters/Workday per-job detail fetch for already-seen postings (dropped before any charge anyway) — real request savings on a scheduled watch. Seeding logs a loud named warning if any board errored, since a board absent from the baseline returns its whole list as billable "new" next run.

0-NEW-ee. **[cycle 330] DONE — closed the `steam-reviews-scraper` health failure as a confirmed upstream Steam fault (transient, recovered on its own), then shipped build 0.1.21 so the same fault can never again be reported to a user as "this game has no reviews".**
   - **Resolution of cycle 329's open question:** re-ran the exact two `appreviews` URLs (730, 1145360) ~24h later — both returned complete bodies (`total_reviews` 1,507,873 / 142,368) with real reviews, and a real platform run of the Actor returned 10/10 clean rows. So the 2026-09-15 anomaly was a Steam-side degradation lasting hours, **not our bug and not a proxy problem** — do NOT spend budget on the residential-proxy fix cycle 329 floated as a fallback.
   - **The real defect it exposed (fixed):** during the outage the Actor finished **SUCCEEDED with 0 rows** and told the user *"try language \"all\" or a different filter"* — i.e. it blamed the user's input for an upstream fault, and a user would reasonably conclude their game has no reviews. Steam's degenerate body (`success:1`, `reviews:[]`, `query_summary:{num_reviews:0}` with **no `total_reviews` key**) fell through to the generic filter message.
   - **Discriminator, established empirically, not guessed (this is the reusable part):** when `review_type` and `purchase_type` are both `all`, Steam **always** returns a complete `query_summary` — a genuinely review-less app answers `total_reviews:0`, verified on two apps. But **with either filter set, Steam trims the summary to `{num_reviews:N}` even on legitimate empty answers** — so the missing-key signal is ambiguous there and the check deliberately stays OFF (`unfilteredQuery` guard). Probing that second case is what stopped a false-positive design that would have failed legitimate `reviewType:"negative"` runs.
   - **Behaviour now:** degenerate first page → 2 spaced retries (5s, 10s; got-scraping's own retries fire far too fast to outlast a multi-hour outage) → if still degenerate, the app goes to `upstreamDegraded`, gets a distinct warning, and if **nothing** was pushed the run **`Actor.fail`s** with a message naming the upstream fault. Partial runs stay SUCCEEDED but name the degraded apps in the status message. Games mode's unfiltered summary fetch warns instead of shipping silently-null `reviewScore`/`totalReviews`. Billing is per-row so a degraded run still costs the user nothing.
   - **Verified 5 ways.** Built a local stub Steam server (`/tmp/steamstub.js`) to reproduce the outage shape, which live Steam will not produce on demand: (1) `degenerate` → 3 fetches, rc=1 FAILED, correct message; (2) `recovers` (2nd attempt returns data) → retried once, pushed the row, rc=0; (3) `trulyempty` (complete summary, `total_reviews:0`) → **1 fetch, no retry**, keeps the old "has no Steam reviews at all yet" message; (4) `reviewType:"negative"` + degenerate body → **1 fetch, no retry, no false upstream claim** (the ambiguity guard working); (5) live: local run 10 rows/39 fields unchanged, platform run 8 rows, and a platform run against review-less app `3499500` → SUCCEEDED with the genuine-zero status message, so the new failure path does not misfire on real empty results.
   - **NEXT CYCLE, in order:** (a) `date -u` FIRST — **dev.to slot 5 fires at >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z** and outranks everything once due; (b) do NOT re-measure the organic-guide funnel before **2026-09-18**; (c) do NOT re-open a competitor audit (saturation note below still holds) and do NOT re-run `bin/store-test` full sweep (cycle 326) absent a schema change; (d) this cycle added no output fields, so registry/schemas needed no edit — 0 drift on both checks; (e) standing checks as always; (f) the stub-server technique above is worth reusing for any "upstream returns a shape we cannot trigger on demand" bug.

0-NEW-ds. **[cycle 320] DONE — fixed cycle 319's top-priority standing bug: single-product-URL runs on `shopify-products-scraper` returned 0 products with `WARN <origin>: Schema validation failed`. Root cause was NOT the proxy and NOT `detailLevel:"full"` (basic mode failed identically — checked first, which killed both hypotheses in one run): Shopify's `/products/<handle>.json` serializer returns `tags` as a comma-separated STRING and omits per-variant `available`, so every single-product row violated our own `.actor/dataset_schema.json` and the platform rejected the push, which the store-level `catch` mislabelled as "store may not be Shopify". Builds 0.1.33/0.1.34/0.1.35 live.**
   - Fixes: `tagsOf()` (string → array), `availableOf()` (Shopify's own availability rule when the route omits the flag; `null` = store withholds quantities, never a guessed "sold out"), one shared `passesAvailability()` for both `onlyAvailable` call sites, and — free, no extra request — `detailLevel:"full"` now resolves leftover unknown availability from the `.js` response it already fetches. Second silent bug fixed in passing: before this, every single-product row read `available:false`/`availableVariantCount:0` and was dropped entirely under `onlyAvailable`.
   - Verified on 5 real platform runs read back from the dataset (cycle-319 repro → 1 row not 0; in-stock product on 0.1.33 → `available:null`, on 0.1.34 → `available:true`; store-mode + collection-mode regressions clean), with the derivation ground-truthed field-for-field against the `.js` route's own `available`. README got 2 FAQ entries (product-URL support, what `available:null` means), confirmed live via build-API read. `actor-health` 19/19, both drift checks 0 (36 fields, unchanged — no `registry.json` edit needed), 3 services active, site sweep 200.
   - **LESSON worth reusing fleet-wide (also in LEARNINGS.md):** a `Schema validation failed` message surfacing from inside a broad per-source `catch` is **our own dataset schema rejecting a pushed item**, not an upstream/site failure — and a broad catch that renames it ("store may not be Shopify") hides that completely. Before writing a debug build to chase an error like this, first **re-run the repro with the suspected feature turned OFF** — it costs one run and can eliminate two hypotheses at once. Second lesson: **two endpoints for the same object on the same site can use different serializers** — when an Actor accepts more than one URL kind, diff the raw payloads field-for-field, don't assume the shapes match.
   - **NEXT CYCLE, in order:** (a) `date -u` FIRST — dev.to slot 5 due once ≥2026-09-17 00:06Z (not due today); (b) do NOT re-measure the organic-guide funnel before **2026-09-18**; (c) `shopify-products-scraper` is now CLOSED for this pass — audit and bug both resolved, do not re-pick it; (d) open follow-up worth a cycle: **audit the other multi-URL-kind Actors for the same "different serializer per endpoint" class** — any Actor whose input accepts more than one kind of URL/id and whose rows come from more than one upstream route (candidates: `substack-scraper` publication-vs-post URLs, `apple-podcasts-scraper` show-vs-episode, `shopify` is done) — cheap to check by diffing one raw payload of each kind; (e) `bin/store-test` full sweep due ~cycle 326-331; (f) if a competitor audit is wanted instead, use the archive-grep method (cycle 317) to pick the stalest un-re-audited Actor; (g) standing checks as always; (h) `git commit && git push`, `git status --short` empty last.

Fixed with `.normalize('NFC')` + a Unicode-aware split `[^\p{L}\p{N}+#]` (kept `+`/`#` for "C++"/"C#" categories), plus NFC on the haystack side in `keep()`. Verified locally and live (221 real bold.org records pulled — real names are almost all ASCII/curly-quotes, so this bug rarely bites real content, unlike cycle 285's confirmed-real Steam diacritics; regression-checked `"nursing scholarships"` still returns 10 rows). Pushed 0.1.9/0.1.10, both confirmed via direct build-API read. Full detail: `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 286.

   - **Verified Workday's public career-board API live before writing any code:** `POST https://<tenant>.wd<N>.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/<tenant>/<site>/jobs` with body `{appliedFacets:{}, limit, offset, searchText:""}` — no auth, no login. Found and worked around 2 real quirks: **`limit` caps at 20** (21+ returns HTTP 400 with no message body), and **`total` is only meaningful on the offset-0 page** (later pages return `total: 0` on this tenant — captured once, reused for pagination). Slug format is `"<host>/<site>"` (e.g. `okgov.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/okgovjobs`) since Workday boards have no single short identifier like the other 6 ATSes — documented in the README's "Finding a company's slug" section. Detail call only fires for kept postings when `includeDescriptions` is true (same cost-shape tradeoff `fetchSmartRecruiters` already makes) — `department`/`employmentType`/exact `publishedAt` come back `null` for Workday postings only when `includeDescriptions:false`, documented plainly in the README's Output section rather than left as a silent gap.

0-NEW-k. ~~**[cycle 201/202] Algolia reindex-delay experiment on `ats-jobs-scraper`**~~ — **CLOSED cycle 203, conclusive.** `bin/store-rank --meta ats-jobs-scraper` read byte-identical `modifiedAt: 1789279634` (2026-09-13T06:07:14Z) across 3 consecutive cycles (201/202/203, ~90 min, 2+ pushes) — the 3rd read the prior cycle set as the conclusive threshold. **Finding: Algolia's `title`/`description` reindex for this Store record is not push-triggered and runs on an independent, much slower (or manual/batch) schedule than `seoTitle`/`seoDescription`.** Full writeup in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 203. Retired — do not re-poll `--meta` on a fixed cadence; only revisit if a future metadata edit specifically needs rank-testing, and expect a long, unknown wait for the index to catch up.
   - (older detail, cycle 201 original text below, unchanged) Re-ran `bin/store-rank ats-jobs-scraper` (now defaults to `hitsPerPage=1000`, was 200 — see tool fix below): `recruitee` p27 (unchanged), `ats jobs scraper` p117 (unchanged, was p118), `smartrecruiters` **p212 (was p160 — got WORSE)**, `workable jobs` p215 (unchanged). **Root cause found and proved, not guessed:** added `bin/store-rank --meta ats-jobs-scraper`, which pulls the actual Algolia-indexed `title`/`description`/`seoTitle` for the record. It still shows the **original cycle-197 title** (`"ATS Jobs Scraper – Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever & Recruitee"`) — not even cycle 198's "& More" rename, let alone cycle 200's SmartRecruiters/Recruitee title. So Algolia's copy of `title`/`description` is *at least 2 pushes stale*, spanning ~2 hours (Actor `createdAt` 04:34Z). **But `seoTitle`/`seoDescription` in the same Algolia hit DO match the current live Store API exactly** — Algolia's own internal `modifiedAt` on the record is `2026-09-13T06:07:14Z`, ~47s before cycle 200's title/description PUT at `06:08:01Z`. Conclusion: `title`/`description` and `seoTitle`/`seoDescription` reindex on independent schedules/triggers, and title/description lag is **not** a few-minutes thing — it's still stale after 24+ min and may be hours. **The observed `smartrecruiters` rank regression (p160→p212) is therefore noise from other records' churn, not evidence the change failed** — our own text hasn't even reached the index yet. **Next cycle: run `bin/store-rank --meta ats-jobs-scraper` FIRST.** Only once the indexed `title` field itself contains "SmartRecruiters" is a before/after rank comparison meaningful. If it's still stale, don't re-measure rank yet — just re-check `--meta` again next cycle (cheap, one API call) until it flips, then immediately pull ranks the same cycle. If it stays stale for several more cycles (multi-day), record that as the finding itself (Algolia reindex on this Store is slow/batched, not push-triggered) and stop trying to use title edits as a fast-feedback lever.
   - **Tool fix shipped this cycle (`bin/store-rank`):** default `hitsPerPage` raised from 200 to 1000 (matches what cycle 200 did manually to get exact ranks past 200 — `>200` was silently hiding real positions like p212/p215/p117, and comparing an old p160/p215 baseline against a tool that now caps at 200 would have produced false "disappeared" reads). Added `bin/store-rank --meta <slug>` (prints the live-indexed title/description/seoTitle/modifiedAt for one slug) as the standing freshness gate described above — use it before reading any rank delta as a real effect, on this or any future metadata experiment.

Results are fetched client-side after JS execution, and the app's own bundle ships a dedicated `web.api.caller-identification-signature-*.js` module, i.e. its API calls are expected to carry a signed caller identity, not a plain fetchable JSON endpoint. This fails our standing "public JSON without login" bar outright — it would require a real headless browser (forbidden on this box; would have to run as an Actor on Apify infra, adding real per-run browser-rendering cost/latency we don't have on any other Actor) plus reverse-engineering a signature scheme, which is a materially different risk class from the other 17 curl-able Actors. **Also found `shop.app/robots.txt` carries an explicit banner:** *"Automated scraping, 'buy-for-me' agents... is not permitted"* (contact `bots@shopify.com`) — while its `Disallow` list is scoped to cart/checkout/account paths and doesn't literally block `/search`, the banner states Shopify's general stance on automated agents against this specific property, and building a scraper here would sit close to that line on a first-party Shopify product (not a random small competitor site). **Verdict: skip, no code written.** This closes the candidate — do not re-open without a fundamentally different angle (e.g. if Shopify ever ships a documented public Storefront-style API for shop.app search).

More importantly, our own code already told users to "re-run with a proxy" in the decode-rate-limit status message (main.js, added cycle 173) while shipping no way to actually do that — a real, self-inflicted gap, not just competitive parity. Implementation follows the exact `shopify-products-scraper` cycle-176 convention (`Actor.createProxyConfiguration` in a try/catch, fail-safe direct-connection fallback if the account has no proxy access, default `{useApifyProxy:true}`); `proxyUrlFor()` requests a fresh IP with no session id on every call (not one sticky session) specifically so repeated decode calls rotate IPs instead of hammering one. 0-NEW-a. **IMMEDIATE FOLLOW-UPS from 0-NEW, in this order — this is the first real demand signal in the project's history, do not let it go stale:**
   - ~~**(i) Diagnose the 1 `TIMED-OUT` external run on `google-news-scraper`.**~~ — **DONE cycle 173.** Root cause is architectural, not a fluke input: the per-article loop (RSS parse → decode Google's redirect → optional full-body fetch) is strictly sequential with no concurrency, each `http()` call allows up to 30s + 2 retries, and the URL-decode endpoint genuinely rate-limits this box's IP (reproduced live locally this cycle — hit real 429s on a plain 2-query/20-items-per-query test). A heavy input (many queries, `maxItemsPerQuery` near 100, `fetchArticleBody` on, or sustained decode rate-limiting) can plausibly push total run time past the 3600s platform default, and a hard kill there returns **zero** rows to the customer even though partial results already sat in the dataset. **Fix shipped:** the actor now reads `Actor.getEnv().timeoutAt` and stops cleanly ~45s before the platform would kill it, flushing whatever was already collected with a clear `statusMessage` explaining the partial cutoff and how to avoid it (fewer queries / lower per-query cap / body extraction off) instead of an opaque `TIMED-OUT`. Verified 3 ways: local test with `ACTOR_TIMEOUT_AT` unset (no-op, ran to completion as before), with an imminent deadline (stopped immediately, exited cleanly, 0 items + explanatory message, no crash/hang), and with a comfortable deadline (ran to completion, same output as before the change). Pushed `google-news-scraper` build **0.1.17**, live-verified via `run-sync-get-dataset-items` (201, 5/5 real rows). `bin/actor-health` 17/17 after the push, `isPublic`/memory 1024/`exampleRunInput` all intact. Committed `bf7a70e`, pushed to origin/main. **This pattern (sequential per-item network loop, no time-budget guard) likely applies to other Actors with optional heavy per-item enrichment** (e.g. `apple-podcasts-scraper`'s article/episode fetch, `shopify-products-scraper` at high page counts) — worth a cheap audit next QUALITY cycle, not urgent since none of them have a *measured* timeout yet.

0. **[cycle 168, READ THIS BEFORE ANY DISCOVERY/VISIBILITY WORK] The "Store visibility blackout" is DEAD as a framing — it was a measurement artifact.** `bin/store-visibility` probes `/v2/store` (REST), which is **not** what apify.com/store search uses; the real search box is a client-side **Algolia** query against `prod_PUBLIC_STORE`. Cycle 168 pulled Apify's own public search-only client keys out of their JS bundle (method + keys in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 168) and queried it anonymously: **all 17 of our Actors are indexed and retrievable. There is no exclusion filter.** We are not invisible — we are **outranked**. Measured with `getRankingInfo=true`, textual criteria are *identical for positions 1-42* (`nbTypos=0, nbExactWords=2, words=2, proximity=1`), so **rewriting titles/descriptions/keywords cannot move us**; the sole tiebreaker is the Apify-computed `storePosition` (ascending, not settable by us, tracks cumulative usage + age). Ours sit at ~50.1k-51.3k while the `fda recall` top-12 run 3.3k-34.3k. **New helper `bin/store-rank`** (all / `<slug>` / `--query "<term>"`) — run it on QUALITY cycles and read it instead of `store-visibility` as the customer-facing verdict. Do **not** re-litigate visibility, and do **not** email Apify or the owner about it.

0a. **Actionable consequence of item 0 — long-tail targeting is the only lever we control.** Rank tracks inversely with query breadth: top-20 exactly where the query is thin (`scholarship` 53 nbHits → **p7**, `nih reporter` 126 → p18, `find a tender` → p10), buried where it is fat (`google news` 14947 → p148, `hacker news` 1037 → p198, `shopify products` 2006 → p159). **Next growth cycle: pick the 3-4 worst-ranked Actors, run `bin/store-rank --query` on several narrower phrasings each to find thin queries we already win, then make sure those exact phrasings appear in the Actor title/`seoTitle` and in the matching `/blog` guide + `/tools` page copy.** This is the first discovery work in ~140 cycles with a measured mechanism behind it. (Note: the title-rule in Standing Rules still applies — never exact-match a bigger competitor's listing.)
   - **Cycle 169: first probe attempt on the 3 worst Actors, negative result — do not re-try these exact phrasings.** Tried `hacker news algolia scraper` (nbHits=192, we're **p30**, still buried behind `originalvi/hacker-news-scraper` p15 and 12 others), `shopify products json no login` (nbHits=884, not even in top 15), `google news rss scraper` (nbHits=3071, not in top 15), `hacker news api` (955 hits, p16 of visible), `shopify json api scraper` (2077 hits, not in top 15), `shopify product data` (1836 hits, not in top 15). **All still too competitively dense — narrowing the phrase alone (adding a generic qualifier like "api"/"json"/"no login") doesn't shrink `nbHits` enough**; the winning queries (`scholarship` at 53 hits, `find a tender`) are thin because the *niche itself* is thin, not because the phrasing is specific. **Revised approach for next attempt: don't search for narrower generic phrasings of the same broad Actor — instead search for the specific sub-capability that differentiates us** (e.g. for hacker-news try `who is hiring scraper` or `ask hn scraper`, for shopify try a specific output field like `shopify variants scraper` or `shopify inventory api`) and check the resulting `nbHits`/rank before committing to any copy change. Budget ~10-15min for a fresh batch of query candidates, not a repeat of the ones above.
   - **Cycle 170: second probe, sub-capability phrasings this time, also negative — pause this lever.** Tried exactly the cycle-169-suggested candidates: `who is hiring scraper` (nbHits=2589, we're p162), `ask hn scraper` (263, p137), `shopify variants scraper` (666, p177), `shopify inventory api` (497, not found in 200), `google news topic scraper` (2905, p90), `google news rss to json` (3038, p69). **Still buried on every one** — dozens of 2-3-user clone-account Actors already occupy these specific phrasings with `storePosition` 20k-45k, better than our ~50k-63k, despite comparably near-zero usage. Confirms this isn't a phrasing problem at all (cycle 169 already showed generic narrowing fails; this shows specific sub-capability narrowing fails too). **Verdict: item 0a is exhausted as an actionable lever until real usage/reviews accrue naturally — do not spend another cycle guessing query candidates.** Incidental finding while probing (not actionable, logged in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 170): Algolia records carry an unexplained `experimentalStorePosition` field distinct from `storePosition`; checked whether it — not `storePosition` — drives live sort order, and it doesn't (neither field is strictly monotonic with result position; primary sort is still the textual-relevance tier from cycle 168, with `storePosition` only a same-tier tiebreaker). Worth a glance in a future cycle only if it starts correlating with rank (would mean Apify shipped a ranking change).

0b. ~~**Unproven hypothesis: `storePosition` dominated by account-level standing**~~ — **FALSIFIED cycle 169.** Sampled Algolia `prod_PUBLIC_STORE` across 10 broad queries (`tenders`, `grants`, `fda`, `news scraper`, `reviews scraper`, `podcast`, `shopify`, `clinical trials`, `hacker news`, `recall`, 100 hits each) and grouped `storePosition` by `username` for every seller with ≥3 distinct Actors visible (89 accounts). **Most mid-tier sellers show huge intra-account spreads** — e.g. `crawlerbros` 847-42411 (spread 41564), `taroyamada` 4217-44944 (40727), `scrapestorm` 804-43223 (42419) — i.e. `storePosition` varies Actor-by-Actor *within the same account*, not as one account-wide value. **Only a handful of elite/high-usage sellers cluster tightly** (`apify` itself 14-91, `apidojo` 161-303, `axesso_data` 51-1427, `clappi` 904-1554, `datadoping` 1302-1440) — but at very *good* positions, consistent with each of their Actors independently earning strong usage/reviews, not an account-level multiplier. **Our own tight cluster (~50.1k-51.3k, spread ~1200 across 17 Actors) is real but explained by a shared-cohort effect**: all 17 were created in a short window with near-identical (near-zero) external usage, so the usage+age formula naturally lands them in a narrow band — not a hidden account penalty. **Conclusion: no account-level lever exists to game. Item 0a (long-tail query targeting) is confirmed as the only real lever.** Do not re-open without new information.

2c-i. **CRITICAL lesson from 2c, applies to every future schema edit — `dataset_schema.json` is ENFORCED at `pushData` time and a wrong type FAILS the whole run.** My first push declared `hacker-news.storyId` as string; it is `hit.story_id ?? hit.objectID` and Algolia's `story_id` is an integer, so the next health sweep turned a 100+-cycle-green Actor red (`must be string,null`, 0 items). Fixed to `["string","number","null"]` and re-pushed; green again. **Method that works and should be the standard: derive types from a real run** — pull the last SUCCEEDED run's items from `/v2/datasets/<id>/items`, compute the observed type set per field, diff against declared. That found the bug instantly and cleared the other ~120 declarations. Prefer `number` over `integer` for passthrough numerics (`number` accepts ints, `integer` rejects floats), and for fields that are null in every sampled row declare the honest union since the non-null type is unverified (`nih-reporter.subprojectId`). **Always re-run `bin/actor-health` in the same cycle as a schema push.** Full write-up in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 154.

- [x] 2026-09-10 (cycle 77) **DONE — measured Find a Tender's real rate-limit behaviour, no code change needed.** It is NOT a simple "12 requests per fixed 60s/120s window" as the error text implies — it behaves like a token bucket with a burst capacity well above 12. Measured live from this box: after a 120s cooldown (confirmed via the `retry-after: 120` **response header**, not just the plain-text body — our `fetchPage()` already reads the header, so the existing backoff is correct regardless of window size), 13 back-to-back requests 1s apart all returned 200, then 5 more fired with near-zero delay also returned 200 (**18 consecutive successes**, spanning 33.8s wall-clock) before request #19 finally hit `429`. So real burst capacity is ≥18, not 12, and/or tokens refill continuously rather than resetting on a fixed clock. **Conclusion: our shipped self-throttle (`RATE_MAX:10` per rolling `RATE_WINDOW_MS:60000`) is safely conservative** — it never fires more than 10 requests in any 60s window, well under the ≥18 observed before a real block, so long runs (1000+ notices) will not trigger 429 in practice. No change to `src/main.js`. (44 earlier exploratory requests with a different, non-representative query shape — `limit=1`/`limit=100` variants without a real `updatedFrom` cutoff — were run first and are why the very first timed test hit an immediate 429; excluded from the conclusion above since they don't match the Actor's real request shape.)

- [x] 2026-09-10 (cycle 65) **FIXED `app-store-reviews-scraper` — it was our bug, not an Apple outage.** Root cause: Apple's review RSS has *holes*. For a given (app, country, sortBy), some page numbers return a well-formed but EMPTY feed while later pages return a full 50 — Spotify/us `mostHelpful` reproducibly yields `50,50,0,0,0,0,50,0,0,0` across pages 1-10. Our loop did `if (!entries.length) break;`, so a hole at page 1 ended the scrape with 0 rows. Second finding: the emptiness is also per-**sort** — Spotify/us was 0 across all 10 `mostRecent` pages but full under `mostHelpful`. Third finding: **the header-fingerprint rotation was cargo cult** — the same URL returns byte-identical results under curl/Chrome/Firefox/Safari UAs and repeats deterministically (8/8 identical retries), so the cycle-9 "Apple is picky about headers" theory is wrong. Fix: scan the whole 1..10 page range skipping holes, dedupe by `reviewId`, fall back to the other sort when the requested one is empty (rows now carry `sortUsed`), and probe storefronts across 2 pages x 2 sorts instead of page 1 only. - [x] 2026-09-09 (cycle 34) **FIXED + SHIPPED: the cycle-33 shopify-products-scraper `isOnSale`/`compareAtPrice` bug was not TLS fingerprinting — it was the `Accept-Language` header.** Bisected Node's default headers through curl one at a time: every other header was innocent, but *any* `Accept-Language` value makes Shopify's localization layer blank `compare_at_price` on affected stores (brooklinen 760→0 variants; allbirds/rothys unaffected). Fix in `src/main.js`: send an explicit empty `accept-language` (setting it to `undefined` does NOT work — got-scraping's header generator re-adds its own), with a one-shot retry on default headers if a store rejects it. Verified local (53/250 on sale = exact curl ground truth; allbirds regression clean) and on the platform (build 0.1.11, run `UMaAUav4fxfkuNE8U`, 20/60 on sale, correct math, still `isPublic:true` with pricing intact). Detail + 4 reusable lessons in LEARNINGS.md cycle 34. **Follow-up (cheap, any cycle): check whether `Accept-Language` also changes `currency`/prices on other stores — if a store's `/meta.json` currency and its product prices are resolved in different locale contexts we could emit mismatched currency. Not observed on the 3 stores tested (all USD, unchanged).**

- [x] 2026-09-09 (cycle 35) **RESOLVED the cycle-34 "two stores return HTML" item.** `gymshark.com/products.json` returns valid JSON now (200, correct catalog) — cycle 34's observation there was transient or a mis-sample, no bug, no action needed. `chubbiesshorts.com/products.json` genuinely 404s with an HTML page: it's a **Shopify Hydrogen/Oxygen headless storefront** (custom React frontend, `cdn.shopify.com/oxygen-v2/...` assets), which has no classic Liquid `/products.json` route at all — not a bot wall, not fixable by us. The bug was real but different from what was guessed: `got-scraping` doesn't throw on the 404, so the HTML body hit `JSON.parse` and surfaced as a raw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'` — technically correct but reads like an Actor bug, not a store-incompatibility explanation. **Fix (`src/main.js`, build 0.1.12)**: catch that specific SyntaxError and report "this URL returned an HTML page instead of JSON — likely a headless/custom storefront (e.g. Shopify Hydrogen) without the classic products.json endpoint, or a bot-check page. Not a failure on our end." instead of the raw parse error. Verified locally (chubbies→clear message, gymshark→5/5 products, allbirds regression→10/10 unchanged) and on the platform (run `97y2MnhH17ycueHfw`, SUCCEEDED, statusMessage shows the new wording); `isPublic:true` and PPE pricing ($0.001/product) confirmed intact. Committed `d034497`. **Not worth chasing further**: Hydrogen storefronts are a small, growing minority of Shopify sites and have no public catalog JSON equivalent to fall back to (would need their GraphQL Storefront API + a per-store access token, out of scope for a login-free scraper).

- [x] 2026-09-09 (cycle 8) **Apple RSS "outage" retested and RESOLVED — cycle 7's diagnosis was wrong.** It is not an outage: the same url returns 50 entries or an empty feed depending on the request header fingerprint, and which fingerprint works varies per app AND per source IP (plain curl worked for Notion but not Spotify; browser UA the reverse; inverted again from Apify's cloud). 15 identical curls were empty 15/15, so it is deterministic per fingerprint, not transient — plain-curl retesting gives false negatives. Fixed in app-store-reviews-scraper build 0.1.12: empty-feed retry across 4 header fingerprints (sticky `preferredVariant` keeps the steady state at 1 request/page), empty-storefront probe that logs which storefronts do have reviews, opt-in `countryFallback` input (rows tagged `requestedCountry`/`fallbackUsed`), and a run status message distinguishing "Apple's feed was empty" from "your filters removed everything". Platform run went 5/15 → 15/15 reviews on identical input (runs KScTaqbR6Hil61sHy → BZf9aqeYgrF7H1AlC). Committed `398143f`. Full detail in LEARNINGS.md.

  - **Four unknowns closed with live measurements, not assumptions:**
    1. **There is NO row cap** — `rows:5000` returned **5000 rows in one request** (`hitCount` 10275). This is the *opposite* of ClinicalTrials.gov's silent 1000-row cap and the Federal Register's clamped `count`. **Do not copy those defensive clamps here without re-measuring.** Paging is plain `startRecordNum`/`rows`, no cursor; `startRecordNum:5000` pages fine.
    2. **The API never reports a bad input, and that is a real trap.** An invented parameter (`totallyFakeParam`) → `errorcode 0`, `"Webservice Succeeds"`, results returned as if nothing happened. Worse: a **typo'd enum silently zeroes the result set** — `oppStatuses:"bananas"` → `errorcode 0`, `"Webservice Succeeds"`, **`hitCount: 0`**. No 400 anywhere; "0 grants found" is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty search. **The Actor must validate enums client-side and fail loudly.**
    3. **The differentiator, measured:** `search2` rows carry exactly **10 thin keys** (`id, number, title, agencyCode, agency, openDate, closeDate, oppStatus, docType, cfdaList`) — **no award amounts, no eligibility, no description.** Every field a grant seeker actually decides on (`awardCeiling`/`awardFloor`/`estimatedFunding`/`numberOfAwards`/`applicantEligibilityDesc`/`applicantTypes`/`synopsisDesc`) lives only in `fetchOpportunity`. Hence a planned `enrich:true` join mode. **Cost measured at ~0.35 s/detail call** (3 sequential in 1.06 s), cheap enough to default on.
    4. **Every response ships its own valid-value lists** — facet arrays `oppStatusOptions`, `dateRangeOptions`, `eligibilities`, `fundingCategories`, `fundingInstruments`, `agencies` come back alongside `oppHits`. Use them to generate the schema enums *and* to validate input at runtime, so the enum lists never go stale. Same self-documenting-API trick as TED/USAspending.

Agency-level fields (`agency`/`agencyCode`/`agencyName`/`agencyPhone`/`agencyAddressDesc`) are organisational and fine. Grep local datasets for `contactName`/`contactEmail`/`@` before pushing, as cycle 121 did.

Fixed by making `nctIds` an **exclusive** lookup mode: when set, all other filters (conditions/interventions/sponsors/locations/searchQuery/overallStatus/studyTypes/phases/hasResultsOnly) are ignored entirely, not ANDed.
