All webhookUrl POST calls are deliberately bare-but-caught (warning-only, by design). Checked every remaining hit's caller, not just the call site itself, since a bare call wrapped by its *caller's* try/catch is just as safe as one wrapped inline:
     - `steam-reviews-scraper`, `apple-podcasts-scraper`, `app-store-reviews-scraper`, `substack-scraper`, `hacker-news-scraper`, `fec-campaign-finance-scraper`: every per-item/per-page call site is already individually try/catch-wrapped with a graceful degrade (warn + return null/skip/continue) — confirmed by reading each one, not assuming from the `retry:{limit:N}` option alone. **Genuinely already safe, no gap.**
     - `ats-jobs-scraper`'s bare `getJson` (6 call sites, one per ATS type) looked unwrapped at first glance, but the whole per-company loop is wrapped one level up (`try { result = await FETCHERS[ats](slug) } catch (e) { ...erroredCompanies.push...; continue; }`) — a fetch failure for one company is already skipped, not fatal. **Already safe.**
     - `scholarship-scraper` was the one real gap: `fetchHtml` (bare `gotScraping`, native `retry:{limit:2}`, `throwHttpErrors:false` so it only degrades HTTP errors to null) is called once per discovered/pasted URL inside the main crawl loop, with **no try/catch around the call site or its caller** — after native retries exhaust on a network-level error (timeout/ECONNRESET/DNS), the throw propagated past the per-URL loop into the outer `catch` block, which calls `Actor.fail()` for the **whole run**, discarding scholarships already pushed (and charged) from earlier URLs in the same run. Same bug class as h68/h69, just in a `for (const url of urls)` loop instead of a hand-rolled attempt-counter loop.
   - **Fix** (`actors/scholarship-scraper/src/main.js`): wrapped the per-URL `fetchHtml(url)` call in try/catch; a thrown network error now logs `<url> — request failed (<message>), skipping this page.`, adds the URL to a new `erroredUrls` list, and `continue`s to the next URL instead of failing the run. A summary line (`Fetch errors (skipped, run not failed): ...`) is logged after the loop, matching the fleet's existing `erroredCompanies`/`notFoundCompanies` convention (ats-jobs-scraper). Build 0.1.13 live.
   - **Verified with fault injection** (cycle-444 recipe): local run with `startUrls` = one real bold.org URL + one `http://127.0.0.1:9/dead-page/` (instant ECONNREFUSED) — WARN fired for the dead URL, the real URL's 16 scholarships were still pushed, run exited 0 with "Done. Also ran the plain stock regression before and after (local 25/25 rows unchanged; platform build 0.1.13 `run-sync-get-dataset-items` on the real `test_input.json` returned 25/25 rows, byte-matching). No output field changed → all 7 standing checks re-run 0 drift, no publish slot spent (internal reliability fix, no README/schema change needed).

Worth a 2-line polish if a future cycle is in this file anyway, not worth its own cycle.

   - (b) genuine offset/page-number params sent by the Actor itself — tested each **directly against the live API with curl** (2 small requests, distinct `page`/`offset` values, diffed the returned identity field — no Actor code run, no Apify cost): `grants-gov-scraper` (`startRecordNum` 0 vs 5) — 10 distinct opportunity IDs, honored. `us-federal-awards-scraper` (`page` 1 vs 2) — 10 distinct award IDs, honored. `nih-reporter-scraper` (`offset` 0 vs 5) — 10 distinct `appl_id`, honored. `fda-recall-scraper` (`skip` 0 vs 5) — 10 distinct recall numbers, honored. `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` (`page` 1 vs 2) — 10 distinct publication numbers, honored. `hacker-news-scraper` (Algolia `page` 0 vs 1) — 10 distinct objectIDs, honored. `ats-jobs-scraper` (Workday `offset` 0 vs 5, live tenant `okgov.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com`) — 10 distinct job IDs, honored (the `total:0` on page ≥1 is the already-documented quirk, not this bug). `substack-scraper` (`offset` 0 vs 5, live `astralcodexten.substack.com`) — 10 distinct post IDs, honored.
   - **Two Actors turned out to already have this exact bug pre-caught by a dedup guard**, found while reading the code around their paging loops rather than needing a live test: `steam-reviews-scraper` has `if (seen.has(r.recommendationid)) continue; // Steam repeats the last page when the cursor runs out` sitting **before** `pushResult()` (the charge call) — confirmed the guard runs pre-charge, not post. `google-play-reviews-scraper` has the identical shape (`seenReviewIds`, comment "Google Play's paginated review endpoint can repeat a row across page boundaries", dedup before `Actor.charge`/`pushData`). Both were presumably fixed in earlier cycles; not a new finding, but confirms the fix is real and in the charge-gating position, not just cosmetic.

0-NEW-h249. **[cycle 628] DONE (BUILD-slot — read `substack-scraper` source end-to-end and found + fixed a REAL "buyer gets less than advertised" defect: paywalled free-preview bodies were reported as complete articles). Build 0.1.30 live, 23 Actors, $0 spend.**
   - `date -u` FIRST: ~03:30Z, 2026-09-22. 3 services active, site 200. Inbox unchanged since cycle 578 (`167b67c5` newest) — no support request, no revenue event.
   - **The bug:** Substack's `/api/v1/posts/<slug>` returns a real `body_html` for most subscriber-only posts — but it's the **free preview**, cut off mid-article — while the same response's `wordcount` reports the FULL article length. `bodyTruncated` was computed as `!bodyText`, so a preview with text scored `bodyTruncated: false`. Buyers paid the full-text `result` rate ($0.002/post) for fragments labelled complete. Worst live row: `slowboring.com/how-to-stop-hitler` — 18813 declared words, **693 delivered (3.7%)**, flagged complete.
   - **Fix (build 0.1.30):** ratio detector `!bodyText || (declared>0 && (declared-bodyWords)>=50 && bodyWords < declared*0.9)`, calibrated on 19 live posts across 3 publications (public posts 0.93–1.06 of declared; previews 0.00–0.45 — clean separation).
